questions.q: A web tier behind an ALB must survive the loss of one AZ with no manual action, keep at least 3 instances serving, and scale with traffic. What combination?
options: ASG across >=3 AZs, min 3, target tracking on ALB requests per instance
questions.explanation: ASG spanning >=3 AZs with min size 3 covers AZ loss automatically; target tracking handles elasticity. Single-AZ designs fail the AZ-loss test.

questions.q: A video-processing backend crashes when upload spikes saturate the workers. Which change makes it resilient and loosely coupled?
options: SQS queue between upload and workers with ASG scaling on queue depth
questions.explanation: An SQS buffer decouples ingestion from processing; scaling workers on ApproximateQueueLength absorbs spikes. Vertical sizing doesn't fix load spikes.

questions.q: A globally-served site needs automatic traffic shift to a secondary region when the primary's health check fails. Which Route 53 policy?
questions.explanation: Failover routing primary/secondary with health checks automates region failover. Weighted is for gradual traffic shifting, not automatic failover.

questions.q: RTO must be under 15 minutes for a static site + API, with the lowest possible cost. Which DR strategy?
options: Warm standby with Route 53 failover and replicated data
questions.explanation: Warm standby (scaled-down live copy + data replication + DNS failover) meets a 15-min RTO without active/active cost. Backup/restore RTO is hours.
